newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil states see 18.9-19.1 mln bag coffee crop.
newsitem.headline: Brazil states see 18.9-19.1 mln bag coffee crop.

text.p: A survey of estimates from Brazilian state agricultural bodies suggests that the country's 1997/98 coffee crop will be between 18.9 million and 19.1 million 60-kg bags, Jorge Lobato from the National Coffee Department of the Industry and Commerce Ministry told an international coffee conference.

On Monday the head of the Industry and Commerce Ministry's primary commodities department said that the government was working with a range of between 18 million and 20 million bags for the coming harvest against a 1996/97 crop of 25 million bags.
But both officials stressed the preliminary nature of the figures.
The National Coffee Department is working on a project that would ensure a more objective evaluation of future harvests which could be ready by the end of this year, Lobato said.
"We want to take away all the subjectivity and put in as much objectivity as possible," Lobato said.
A break-down of the 18.9 million to 19.1 million bag range by state follows.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
